metadata.description: Sample character profile demonstrating dual-profile system (historical vs literary)

alternative_names.context: Claimed descent from Han royal family

summary.zh: 刘备，蜀汉开国皇帝，以仁义著称，善于用人，联合东吴抗曹，最终建立蜀汉政权
summary.en: Founder and first emperor of Shu Han. Known for benevolence, skilled at recruiting talent, allied with Eastern Wu against Cao Wei, ultimately established Shu Han regime

personality_traits.source_citation: Book of Shu, Biography of First Ruler
personality_traits.evidence: 善下人，喜怒不形于色 (Good at treating subordinates, did not show anger or joy on his face)
Despite numerous defeats, continued to pursue his ambitions
Successfully recruited Zhuge Liang, Guan Yu, Zhang Fei, and other capable individuals

major_accomplishments.event: Participated in suppression of Yellow Turban Rebellion

major_accomplishments.role: Allied with Sun Quan to defeat Cao Cao
major_accomplishments.significance: Prevented Cao Cao from unifying China
Established territorial base for Shu Han

historical_assessment.contemporary_view: Regarded as legitimate heir to Han Dynasty
historical_assessment.historiographical_view: Successful warlord who capitalized on Han legitimacy claim

summary.zh: 仁德之君，桃园结义，三顾茅庐，托孤白帝，被塑造为理想君主的典范
summary.en: Embodiment of benevolent rulership. Sworn brotherhood at Peach Garden, three visits to Zhuge Liang's cottage, deathbed entrustment at Baidi Castle. Portrayed as model of ideal Confucian ruler

personality_traits.fictional_enhancement: Portrayal emphasizes virtues more than historical records

personality_traits.iconic_scene: Three visits to thatched cottage (三顾茅庐)
Peach Garden Oath with Guan Yu and Zhang Fei

personality_traits.note: Folk saying: '刘备的江山是哭出来的' (Liu Bei's kingdom was cried into existence)

iconic_scenes.description: Sworn brotherhood with Guan Yu and Zhang Fei
iconic_scenes.historical_basis: Relationship existed but oath ceremony likely fictional
iconic_scenes.literary_significance: Establishes theme of loyalty and brotherhood

title.en: Three Visits to the Thatched Cottage

iconic_scenes.description: Liu Bei visits Zhuge Liang three times to recruit him
iconic_scenes.literary_significance: Demonstrates humility and respect for talent

iconic_scenes.description: Liu Bei entrusts his son and kingdom to Zhuge Liang
iconic_scenes.literary_significance: Demonstrates trust and Zhuge Liang's loyalty

fictional_embellishments.element: Supernatural signs at birth and death

cultural_impact.archetype: Benevolent ruler who values righteousness over pragmatism
cultural_impact.popular_perception: Hero of the novel despite ultimate failure

proverbs.en: Liu Bei throws his child - to win hearts

proverbs.zh: 三个臭皮匠，胜过诸葛亮
proverbs.en: Three cobblers equal one Zhuge Liang
proverbs.context: Related to Liu Bei's reliance on advisors

divergences.literary: Idealized Confucian ruler embodying perfect virtue
divergences.explanation: Novel emphasizes Confucian virtues to create moral exemplar

divergences.historical: Controlled, did not show emotions (善怒不形于色)
divergences.explanation: Literary device to create sympathy and demonstrate compassion
Novel focuses on moral character over military success

commonalities: Both sources agree on his ability to attract talented followers
Both emphasize his claim to Han legitimacy
Both acknowledge his ultimate failure to restore Han Dynasty
Both record major biographical events (birth, death, major battles)

relationships.description: Elder sworn brother (by age), lifelong companion
relationships.historical_accuracy: Relationship existed, oath ceremony likely fictional
Relationship existed, oath ceremony likely fictional

relationships.description: Heir and second emperor of Shu Han
Ruler of Eastern Wu, allied against Cao Wei
Founder of Cao Wei, primary rival
